content.value_statement: Agent tools fail when descriptions, schemas, and errors are unclear. This skill provides practical patterns for cleaner tool interfaces and smaller tool sets.
actual_capabilities: Explains how to write tool descriptions that cover purpose, use cases, inputs, outputs, and errors.
Recommends naming and parameter conventions for consistent agent tool collections.
Provides patterns for consolidating overlapping tools into workflow-level interfaces.
Shows how response format options can reduce token use while preserving needed detail.
Outlines evaluation criteria for clarity, completeness, recoverability, efficiency, and consistency.
Includes a helper script for generating and evaluating tool description drafts.
limitations: It gives design guidance, not a production-ready tool server.
It does not validate live MCP servers or execute tool calls.
Its architectural reduction advice assumes strong sandboxing and clear documentation.
Examples are illustrative and need adaptation for each system.

use_cases.title: Design a New Agent Tool
use_cases.description: Create a tool description, schema outline, and error strategy before implementation.

use_cases.title: Consolidate a Tool Set
use_cases.description: Review overlapping tools and decide which workflows should become comprehensive interfaces.

use_cases.title: Document MCP Tool Names
use_cases.description: Standardize fully qualified MCP tool names and examples for agent-facing documentation.

prompt_templates.title: Draft a Tool Description
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the tool-design skill to draft a clear description for a tool named [tool]. Cover purpose, inputs, outputs, errors, and use cases.

prompt_templates.title: Review Tool Clarity
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the tool-design skill to review this tool specification for ambiguity, missing parameters, weak errors, and unclear return values: [paste spec].

prompt_templates.title: Reduce Tool Overlap
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the tool-design skill to compare these tools and recommend consolidation, separation, naming changes, and response format options: [tool list].

prompt_templates.title: Plan Agent Tool Architecture
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the tool-design skill to design an agent tool architecture for [workflow]. Include tool boundaries, namespaces, safety constraints, testing criteria, and documentation needs.

output_examples.input: Review a customer lookup tool description.
output: Identifies vague purpose, missing return details, and weak validation errors.
Suggests a customer ID format, clear usage triggers, and examples of recovery guidance.
Adds concise and detailed response modes for different agent tasks.

output_examples.input: Consolidate calendar availability and event tools.
output_examples.output: Recommends one scheduling workflow tool when availability checks and event creation always happen together. Keeps cancellation separate because it has different risks.

output_examples.input: Design errors for an MCP tool.
output: Defines validation, not found, rate limit, and system error categories.
Adds clear resolution guidance and retry expectations for each category.
Keeps field names consistent across related tools.

best_practices: State what the tool does, when to use it, what it accepts, and what it returns.
Use consistent names, formats, and error structures across related tools.
Test tool descriptions with representative agent tasks before deployment.
anti_patterns: Do not publish vague descriptions that force the agent to guess purpose or scope.
Do not create many overlapping tools for one workflow without clear selection rules.
Do not omit recovery guidance from validation, rate limit, or not found errors.

faq.question: What does this skill help me design?
faq.answer: It helps design agent-facing tool descriptions, schemas, naming conventions, error messages, and tool collection boundaries.

faq.question: Does it implement MCP servers?
faq.answer: No. It gives design guidance and examples for MCP-compatible tool naming and documentation.

faq.question: Can it help reduce a large tool set?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains when to consolidate sequential workflow tools and when to keep tools separate.

faq.question: Does it execute commands or call external services?
faq.answer: No. The skill content is documentation and a helper script; examples do not run by themselves.

faq.question: Which assistants can use it?
faq.answer: The report marks support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: How should I use its architectural reduction advice?
faq.answer: Apply it only when data is well documented, sandboxing is strong, and safety constraints are explicit.
